core.title: Name every wagon verb-object
core.given: A plan contains a wagon slug that will pass through the confirmation phase (CONFIRM)
core.when: The planner chooses or keeps the wagon slug (checked at CONFIRM, confirm-blocking)
core.then: The wagon slug is verb-object: kebab-case, at least two tokens, the leading token a verb from the shared convention verb lexicon, and no connective tokens.
prefer: Lead with an action verb from the shared convention verb lexicon, then the object it acts on
When a wagon slug is a brand or proper-noun name, list it explicitly in the stack's naming-exception list
avoid: Connective tokens in the slug (conjunction-style joiners between words; the checker's token set is authoritative)
Treating a brand or proper-noun slug as implicitly exempt — an unlisted exception is a violation
Adding an ordinary (non-brand, non-proper-noun) slug to the naming-exception list to bypass the rule
unless: The slug is a brand or proper-noun name listed explicitly in the stack's naming-exception list
core.why: A verb-object slug states what the wagon does, keeping wagon names uniform and aligned with the shared verb lexicon; explicit brand exceptions keep deviations visible and reviewable.
evidence: Plan confirmation completes without a wagon-slug naming finding for any wagon in the plan
Any failure reports the offending wagon slug and the reason
Every non-verb-object slug in the plan is a brand or proper-noun name and is listed explicitly in the stack's naming-exception list
verification: Enforced by a naming-pattern check over the wagon slugs named in the plan, run at the plan-confirmation phase (CONFIRM); a finding blocks confirmation (confirm-blocking).

The check tests each wagon slug for: kebab-case; at least two tokens; the leading token in the shared verb lexicon (profile key idiom.verb_lexicon); no connective tokens. A slug failing these tests passes only if it is a brand or proper-noun name explicitly listed in the exception list (profile key enforcement.naming_exception_list); an unlisted (implicit) exception is a violation.

Scope: wagon slugs in the plan only — naming of artifacts that are not wagons (features, WMBTs, acceptances) is covered by other conventions and is not checked here; a plan containing no wagon is not checked.
Severity 3, disposition strict, as declared; no expanded strict policy is asserted.
A failure reports the offending wagon slug and the reason; the concrete finding field names are realization-defined.

fires: The planner introduces a new wagon whose slug will be confirmed
The planner renames a wagon slug
CONFIRM runs over a plan containing any wagon with a single-token, noun-first, non-kebab-case or connective-bearing slug
doesNotFire: Naming of artifacts that are not wagons (features, WMBTs, acceptances) — other naming conventions cover those

proposedKeys.meaning: Location of the stack's shared verb lexicon used for verb-object artifact names; the leading token of a slug must be a verb from this lexicon.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No key in any group names where the shared naming verb lexicon lives; the idiom group covers concrete constructs the core refers to, but none points at the lexicon, which this check needs to test the leading token.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where explicit, reviewable naming exceptions (brand or proper-noun slugs exempt from the verb-object rule) are listed; an unlisted exception is a violation.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: enforcement.suppression_marker covers time-boxed rule suppressions, not a content exception list; no existing key holds where such an explicit exception list lives, and the core's unless-branch needs a stack slot for it.

neutralityNotes: The term 'wagon' is retained in the core because the closed profile vocabulary itself canonizes it as a stack-neutral structure concept (layout.wagon_dir: 'a bounded slice of the product'); a stack using another local name maps it through its profile. 'CONFIRM' is retained as the harness-reported workflow phase name (not a stack, runtime or framework artifact). 'kebab-case' is retained because it is the slug shape the obligation itself mandates, not a stack mechanism. Two concrete anchors could not be neutral and are carried by proposed profile keys: the verb-lexicon location (idiom.verb_lexicon) and the brand-exception list location (enforcement.naming_exception_list). Severity 3 / disposition strict stay with the rule in core:verification per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. Detector, validator, term, finding and test ids, and the rule's example slugs, are bunOnly.
